title: Install Caddy and write the Caddyfile inside LXC 120
runbook:
## Prerequisites

- Container 120 (caddy-proxy) exists on this host
- `<ACME_EMAIL>` — an email address for Let's Encrypt certificate notifications (operator-supplied)

## Run this

```bash
pct start 120
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- apt-get update
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- apt-get install -y caddy
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- mkdir -p /etc/caddy
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- tee /etc/caddy/Caddyfile <<'EOF'
{
	email <ACME_EMAIL>
	admin off
}

aedefrusciohomelab.duckdns.org {
	reverse_proxy 192.168.1.101:8096
}

prowlarr.aedefrusciohomelab.duckdns.org {
	reverse_proxy 192.168.1.102:9696
}

radarr.aedefrusciohomelab.duckdns.org {
	reverse_proxy 192.168.1.103:7878
}

sonarr.aedefrusciohomelab.duckdns.org {
	reverse_proxy 192.168.1.104:8989
}

palworld.aedefrusciohomelab.duckdns.org {
	reverse_proxy 192.168.1.106:8211
}

control.aedefrusciohomelab.duckdns.org {
	reverse_proxy 192.168.1.111:3001
}
EOF
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- systemctl enable --now caddy
```

## Verify

- `pct exec 120 -- caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` prints `Valid configuration`
- `pct exec 120 -- systemctl is-active caddy` prints `active`
- `pct exec 120 -- cat /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` shows the 17-line configuration with all six site blocks

## Rollback

If any step fails, stop and report the error output. To remove Caddy if needed:

```bash
pct exec 120 -- systemctl stop caddy
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- apt-get remove -y caddy
```

```bash
pct exec 120 -- rm -f /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
```
